title: Government Teacher Q&A
subtitle: Questions on the path to Delhi Govt PGT (Economics), with sourced answers

items.q: What do I need to become a Delhi Government PGT (Economics) teacher?
a: You need two things in hand by the **closing date** of a DSSSB ad (eligibility is checked on that date, not on exam day):
- **Qualification:** Master's in Economics / Applied / Business Economics with 50%+ aggregate, AND a B.Ed (or B.A.B.Ed / 3-year B.Ed-M.Ed) from an NCTE-recognised institution.
- **Age:** not over 30. OBC (Delhi) gets +3 years (33), SC/ST +5.
Under the current rules there is no option to join first and finish the B.Ed later.
Pay: Level 8, Rs 47,600 – 1,51,100, Group B. Exam: one tier, 300 marks, 0.25 negative marking.

items.q: Is my OBC certificate valid for DSSSB?
a: **Not as it is, but it's fixable.**
- It's issued by a Delhi Deputy Commissioner's office, but in the **central format** ("for appointment to posts under the Government of India"). DSSSB needs an **OBC (Delhi)** certificate.
- The Delhi High Court ruled in July 2025 (GNCTD v. Nisha) that a certificate meant for central govt posts can't be used for Delhi govt posts.
- Your community is on Delhi's own OBC list, so you qualify. Apply for an OBC (Delhi) certificate at your SDM office / Delhi e-District.
- The non-creamy layer (NCL) part must be recent and issued before the ad's closing date.
- Keep the central certificate: it's the right one for KVS and EMRS (with a fresh central NCL).
Without a valid OBC (Delhi) certificate, DSSSB treats you as General, with an age limit of 30.

items.q: What does 'first division' mean, and does it matter for me?
a: **First division = 60% or more aggregate** in that exam (second: roughly 45-59%, third: roughly 33-44%; exact cut-offs vary by board). If you got a CGPA, use your university's conversion formula.
Under the **old** Delhi PGT rules (used until early 2024), a candidate with first division in Class 12, graduation AND PG could join **without a B.Ed** and finish it within 3 years of joining.
That clause is gone from the current rules. It would matter again only if Delhi restores the old rules, or for NDMC posts if NDMC still uses its old rules (to verify).

sources.title: DSSSB Advt. 01/2014, PGT eligibility incl. first-division clause

items.q: What are the different ways I can become a government PGT Economics teacher?
a: Your Master's in Economics covers the subject. What every route still needs is a **B.Ed** from an NCTE-recognised college (simple: a teaching degree approved by India's teacher-education regulator). CTET is not needed for PGT; it only covers classes 1-8.
The recruitment routes:
- **DSSSB PGT Economics:** Delhi govt schools (Directorate of Education, plus NDMC). Delhi-only posting. Best fit for staying in Delhi.
- **KVS PGT:** Kendriya Vidyalayas (central govt). Transferable anywhere in India. Recent drives run jointly with NVS through CBSE.
- **NVS PGT:** Navodaya Vidyalayas, residential, mostly rural campuses. Hardest on lifestyle.
- **EMRS PGT:** Eklavya Model Residential Schools (NESTS, Ministry of Tribal Affairs), tribal areas across India.
- **State recruitment** (e.g. Uttarakhand UKPSC, Himachal HPRCA): state schools, posting within that state. See Other Routes.
Pay for PGT is Level 8 everywhere: basic Rs 47,600 rising to Rs 1,51,100.

B.Ed options: regular 2-year B.Ed (entrance tests like DU B.Ed, IPU CET). A 1-year B.Ed for postgraduates was announced by NCTE but is not confirmed as started. IGNOU distance B.Ed needs 2 years of teaching experience first, so it does not work for you now.
Rough timeline without a B.Ed: 1-2 years for B.Ed, then the next notification, then a 6-12 month selection cycle, so about **2.5-3.5 years** to actually get posted.
**Correction (checked 2026-10-01):** the "36" age limit for DSSSB is NOT notified. Every official DSSSB PGT ad through Oct 2025 says not over 30 (OBC Delhi 33). See the Age Limits section.

- **Haryana (CRSU Jind; Gurugram/Faridabad/Sonipat colleges):** admission on marks, no entrance test. The online form closed on 10 Sep 2026; physical counselling for vacant seats is expected in October.

items.q: Someone told me the PGT age limit has moved up to 36. Is that true?
a: **No, not as of 1 Oct 2026. It is still 30** (33 for OBC Delhi).
- Every official DSSSB ad since Dec 2024 says 'Not exceeding 30', including 10/2024 (PGT), 01/2025 (PGT) and 06/2025 (TGT).
- New Fine Arts PGT rules notified in May 2026 also say 30.
- In March 2026 the Education Minister said the govt would **consider** 36. No order has followed.
- Many coaching sites still print '36'. That's the old rule mixed into current pages.
If 36 is ever notified: 36 + 3 (OBC Delhi) = 39.

items.q: Show me the document proving 36 used to be the limit.
a: **DSSSB Advt. 07/2023** (22 Dec 2023), PGT Economics (Male), post code 809/23, page 24: "Age Limit **Below 36 years**".
**DSSSB Advt. 02/2020** (2 Jan 2020): every PGT post says "Below 36 years".
36 was last used in an ad that closed on 7 Feb 2024. It applied because those posts had been requisitioned (formally requested by the department) before the new rules came in.

items.q: What has the PGT age limit been since 2005? Was 36 the old norm, and are people fighting the change?
a: **Yes: 36 was the long-standing rule, it was cut to 30 in 2022, and candidates are still pushing back.**
- **1975 - 2012:** 36 (per news sources; no DSSSB ads online from this period).
- **2014, 2017, 2020:** official ads say 36. The 2014 ad includes PGT Economics.
- **Jul 2022:** most PGTs still 36; English and Computer Science already 30.
- **29 Sep 2022:** new Delhi DoE PGT rules cut it to **30**. Protests followed in Oct 2022, and a CAT case was filed in 2023. No reversal.
- **2023 - Feb 2024:** a mix of 36 and 30, depending on when each post was requisitioned. The last 36 was PGT Economics in Advt. 07/2023.
- **Dec 2024 onward:** 30 everywhere.
- **Mar 2026:** the minister says 36 is being 'considered'. **May 2026:** new Fine Arts rules still say 30.

sources.title: ETV Bharat: aspirants protest age-limit cut (Oct 2022)

items.q: How long is the gap between the DSSSB ad and the actual exam?
a: **Between 5.5 and 17 months from the closing date to the exam, and the result has taken over a year after that.**
- **Advt. 02/2020:** closed 13 Feb 2020, exam 17 Jul 2021. 520 days (COVID delay).
- **Advt. 07/2023:** closed 7 Feb 2024, exam 21 Jul 2024. 165 days. Result 9 Sep 2025, 415 days after the exam.
- **Advt. 10/2024:** closed 14 Feb 2025, exam 15 Jul 2026 (postponed). 516 days.
Pattern: ad in late Dec/Jan, closing in mid-Feb, Economics exam in July. Only the **closing date** matters for eligibility.

items.q: Can you get me the PGT Economics question papers for the last 10 years?
a: Found papers from **6 exam years (2014-2024)**, saved as 11 PDFs in `syllabus/previous-papers/` with a README listing each file's source. A full 10 years doesn't exist because DSSSB holds a PGT Economics exam only every 2-3 years.
- 2014 and 2015 (Tier-II): Economics section only, solved (YCT)
- 2018 Male and Female Shift 1: full official papers with answer keys (+ Hindi copy, + solved version)
- 2021 Male + Female: full official papers with keys, straight from dsssb.delhi.gov.in
- 2023 Female Shift 2: full official paper with key (+ solved version)
- 2024 Shift 2: full paper
EMRS PGT papers (2023 and 2025 Tier-I with official key) are in `previous-papers/EMRS/`.

**Trust:** files marked `official-with-key` use DSSSB's own answers. `solved-YCT` files come from a book publisher; explanations useful, answers occasionally wrong. Start timed practice with the full official papers.
**Gaps:** the newest exam (Post Code 829/24) paper isn't public yet (shown only via candidate login). 2023 Male and other 2024 shifts not found online.
open: Download the Post Code 829/24 paper once DSSSB makes it public

items.q: What is the meaning of Shift 1 and Shift 2?
a: A shift is a time slot on exam day. When too many candidates apply for one sitting, DSSSB runs the exam more than once that day:
- **Shift 1:** morning, usually around 9 am-12 noon.
- **Shift 2:** afternoon, usually around 2-5 pm.
You get one shift, printed on your admit card; you don't choose it. **Each shift has a different question paper** (same syllabus, pattern and difficulty), so morning candidates can't leak questions.
**Normalisation (score adjustment):** with several shifts, DSSSB adjusts marks so someone with a slightly harder paper isn't disadvantaged.
For practice, any shift's paper is equally useful. Male and Female PGT Economics are separate posts, so their exams are sometimes on different days.

items.q: Is KVS a good backup if Delhi govt doesn't work out?
a: **Yes, mainly because of age room.**
- **Age:** 40, +3 for OBC = 43. Years more than DSSSB's 33.
- **Needs:** Master's 50%+ and a B.Ed. Uses the **central** OBC certificate with a fresh NCL.
- **Last cycle:** combined KVS + NVS recruitment run by CBSE, notified Nov 2025. Two tiers (Tier I 11 Jan 2026, Tier II 29 Mar 2026). From aggregator sites; check the official ad.
- **Catch:** ads come every 2-3 years, and the post is transferable all-India.

items.q: What is EMRS PGT, and does it fit me?
a: **EMRS = Eklavya Model Residential Schools.** Central govt boarding schools for ST students (Classes 6-12), mostly in tribal districts. Recruiter: NESTS (Ministry of Tribal Affairs); exam run by CBSE.
- **Needs:** Master's in Economics 50%+ (Economics at graduation too) AND B.Ed 50%+. The B.Ed is required.
- **Age:** 40, +3 for OBC = 43. Same window as KVS. Uses the central OBC certificate.
- **Pay:** Level 8 plus 10% special pay on basic.
- **Posting:** anywhere in India, residential duties; requests to change station are not entertained.
- **ESSE-2025:** 155 PGT Economics posts. Tier I qualifying; merit on Tier II (Economics) only.

items.q: How do I become a government PGT Economics teacher in Uttarakhand, and can I apply being from Delhi?
a: The way in is the **UKPSC Lecturer (Pravakta) exam**, for Classes 11-12 in Uttarakhand Government Inter Colleges.
**Last cycle (notified Dec 2025, from aggregator sites, unverified):**
- 808 lecturer posts; **72 Economics in the General Branch** (the one open to men)
- Qualification: Master's in Economics 50%+ AND B.Ed (compulsory)
- Applications: 31-12-2025 to 20-01-2026. No TET needed for lecturers.

**From Delhi: probably yes, but as a General candidate.** State reservation and age relaxation are normally for Uttarakhand domiciles only, so expect no OBC benefit and an age limit of 42. That still gives roughly 10 years of chances once the B.Ed is done. 30% of seats are reserved for Uttarakhand women, which shrinks the open pool a little.
Posting: inside Uttarakhand, often hill districts. Order of steps is the same: **B.Ed first**.
open: Read the domicile clause in the official Dec 2025 UKPSC notification (psc.uk.gov.in)

items.q: Same question for Himachal Pradesh: how do I become a PGT Economics teacher there?
a: **Same kind of post, also needs a B.Ed, and the recruiter seems to have changed.**
- **Up to 2023:** HPPSC recruited "Lecturer (School-New) Economics" for Classes 11-12. The 2023 ad (No. 12/10-2023) had 17 Economics posts.
- **2026:** HPRCA (Hamirpur) ran "Teacher Economics", Post Code 26030, **86 posts**. CBT 06-07-2026, result 10-08-2026, document check 29-08-2026.
- **Eligibility (2023 ad, via aggregators):** Master's in Economics 50%+ AND B.Ed 50%+. **Age 18-45**, the most generous of all your options.

**From Delhi:** likely open to all citizens, but reservation and age relaxation are for HP bonafide residents only, so you'd apply as General. HP rules usually mention "knowledge of customs, manners and dialects of HP" (a standard line, not a test).
**Watch:** HP now hires many recruits as **Job Trainees** (about 2 years on fixed pay before regularisation). Check if it applies to teachers. Posting: within HP, often remote hill areas.
Age 45 means roughly 13 years of chances once the B.Ed is done.
open: Confirm from the official HPRCA ad: post level (PGT?), domicile rule, age limit, job-trainee terms (hprca.hp.gov.in)

items.q: Which government teaching jobs (school and college) can I apply for, from PGT to Assistant Professor?
a: Master list lives in EA Demo/Govt_Jobs_By_Category_Ashish_Pal.xlsx, tab '3 Teaching' (7 posts, prepared 28-30 Sep 2026). Reviewed 2026-10-02: 2 corrections, 6 posts to add.
**College (no B.Ed needed; NET or PhD is the gate):**
- Assistant Professor, Economics: DU colleges/departments, JNU, Jamia and other central universities. Master's 55% (50% for OBC-NCL) + UGC NET, or a PhD. No upper age limit. Academic Level 10.
- Assistant Professor at Delhi state universities (GGSIPU, Ambedkar University Delhi): same UGC rules, each university advertises separately.
- Assistant Professor in state govt colleges via state commissions (UPHESC/UPPSC, HPSC, RPSC, etc.): NET/SET/PhD. Age is usually around 40 + state relaxation; the existing sheet's '~62' looks wrong.
- UPSC teaching posts (e.g. Assistant Professor at NDA / central institutions): NET/PhD, age per advert (usually 35-40 + 3 for OBC).
- Guest / ad-hoc lecturer (DU and others): needs NET; paid per lecture.
- UGC NET JRF (funded PhD): OBC age limit 35, so about 4 more years.
**School PGT (B.Ed required, except NDMC where it can be relaxed):**
- DSSSB PGT, Delhi DoE: age 30, 33 with an OBC (Delhi) certificate. The existing sheet's '36' is wrong for DoE.
- DSSSB PGT, NDMC: below 36 (Advt 07/2023); B.Ed relaxable for first-division candidates. Rare: about 5 posts per cycle.
- KVS / NVS PGT: 40, 43 for OBC.
- EMRS PGT (NESTS): 40, 43 for OBC; all-India residential postings.
- Army Public Schools (AWES CSB): PG + B.Ed with 50% in each; freshers below 40. A society under the Army, not strictly government service.
- Sainik School PGT: PG 50% + B.Ed, age 21-40 per school advert. Society under MoD.
- Other states' PGT/lecturer posts (Haryana, UP, Rajasthan): need B.Ed + the state's eligibility test. Often a domicile advantage for locals.

**Not open (yet):** TGT Social Science (needs B.Ed + CTET + the right graduation subjects); Associate Professor / Professor (need a PhD + 8-10 years of teaching); SCERT/DIET lecturer (usually needs an M.Ed).

items.q: DU Assistant Professor (Economics) vs guest / ad-hoc lecturer: what is the difference, what is the route to a PERMANENT post, how long does it realistically take, and what does it depend on?
a: **Three different things:**
- **Permanent Assistant Professor:** a regular post at Academic Level 10 (Rs 57,700 basic + DA/HRA). Job security, pension (NPS), increments, and promotions up to Professor.

- **Ad-hoc:** fills a vacant post on 4-month terms, renewed again and again. Full workload (about 16 hours/week) but no security. DU replaced most ad-hocs in its 2022-24 permanent drive (about 4,500 ad-hocs; reports said about 70% were displaced in early rounds), so few ad-hoc slots are left.
- **Guest faculty:** paid per lecture (Rs 1,500, capped at Rs 50,000/month), about 8 hours/week max. DU now allows guests only against leave vacancies (maternity, study leave, etc.).

**The route to permanent (DU colleges):** UGC NET in Economics, then apply to every college advert, then a screening score of 50+ (out of 100) gets you called, then **selection on the interview alone** (screening marks carry no weight in the interview).

**Ashish's estimated screening score (based on self-reported first divisions; check against the marksheets):** graduation 60-80% = 19 + PG 60-80% = 23 + NET = 8, total **50**. That is exactly the college floor, so NET alone gets him interviews. With JRF: 52. With a PhD: about 75+. University DEPARTMENTS need 65+, so they are effectively closed without a PhD.

**A trap:** guest/ad-hoc experience earns screening marks only if the pay was at least the UGC minimum basic + DA. Guest pay (max Rs 50,000) is below that, so guest teaching usually adds 0 points. It is still worth doing for teaching practice and contacts.

**Realistic timeline (ESTIMATE):** NET takes 6-18 months (only the top 6% of those who sit the exam qualify; many need 2-3 attempts). From NET to a permanent post: 2-5 years of applying and interviewing if it goes well. If he needs a PhD to stand out, add 4-6 years. A fair overall expectation is 3-8 years, with no guarantee.

**What it depends on:** (1) clearing NET; (2) Economics vacancies, especially the OBC-reserved roster points; (3) interview performance: subject depth, a teaching demo, a research/area of interest; (4) PhD + publications (decisive for departments and many state colleges); (5) the panel's discretion, which is opaque. The 2022-24 displacement of long-serving ad-hocs shows experience alone doesn't decide it.

items.q: How do the perks, benefits and holidays compare: DSSSB (Delhi govt) vs KVS?
a: **Same pay. The differences are location, medical cover, your kids' schooling and workload.**
- **Pay:** both Level 8 (Rs 47,600 - 1,51,100); same DA.
- **HRA:** DSSSB is always the Delhi rate (highest). KVS depends on your city.
- **Pension:** both NPS, no old pension. UPS exists for central staff; whether it covers KVS or Delhi govt is unverified.
- **Medical:** Delhi govt has DGEHS; KVS has **CGHS** in big cities (extended July 2024).
- **Kids' school:** KVS staff children are admitted to any KV at any time, even if the class is full.
- **Summer 2026:** DoE 11 May - 30 Jun (with remedial-class duty 11-23 May); KVS Delhi region 8 May - 16 Jun.
- **Winter:** DoE about 1-15 Jan; KVS 23 Dec - 11 Jan.
- **Workload:** DoE has more outside duties (election/BLO, surveys) and big classes; KVS is more structured.
- **Location:** DSSSB is Delhi for life; KVS can post you anywhere in India.
Items marked unverified in the source file are standard govt rules still to be confirmed.

items.q: What pay will I get as a Delhi PGT when I join, and how much will it grow year on year?
a: **Joining salary, Pay Level 8 (Delhi rates, my calculation, not an official figure):**
- Basic pay: Rs 47,600
- DA at 60% (rate since Jan 2026): Rs 28,560
- HRA at 30% (Delhi): Rs 14,280
- Transport allowance (Rs 3,600 + DA): Rs 5,760
- **Gross: ~Rs 96,200 a month.** Less pension contribution (10% of basic + DA) Rs 7,616, so **take-home ~Rs 88,000**.
Under the new tax regime, income tax should come to roughly zero at this level (my calculation). Coaching sites quote Rs 65-82k take-home, but they use older DA and HRA rates.
**Growth:**
- **Annual increment:** 3% of basic every year (1 Jan or 1 July). Basic reaches roughly Rs 62,000 by year 10.
- **DA:** raised twice a year with inflation, usually 2-4 percentage points each time.
- **8th Pay Commission:** set up Nov 2025, report expected around mid-2027. Estimates of the jump are 17-23%, nothing final.
- **MACP (guaranteed upgrades without promotion):** move to a higher pay level at 10, 20 and 30 years of service if not promoted (central rule; Delhi generally follows it).
**Pension:** new joiners are on NPS (market-linked). The central govt added UPS (50% of last basic after 25 years) from April 2025.

items.q: How much will a PGT (Level 8) salary grow over 10 years after the 8th Pay Commission?
a: **Estimate only. The 8th Pay Commission fitment factor has not been announced.** Base case below uses 1.92, the most-quoted estimate.
- **8th CPC status:** reference date 1 Jan 2026; report due around May 2027; arrears expected from 1 Jan 2026. DA was 60% on 1 Jan 2026 under the 7th CPC and resets to 0 under the 8th.
- **Entry basic:** Rs 47,600 x 1.92 = about **Rs 91,400**.
- **If you join in July 2029:** DA about 21% by then, so gross pay is about **Rs 1.41 lakh/month** (basic + DA + Delhi HRA 24% + TA).
- **Growth engine:** 3% increment every July + DA rising about 6 points a year (tracks inflation). HRA steps up to 27% and 30% as DA crosses 25% and 50%.
- **Year 10 (July 2038):** about **Rs 2.57 lakh/month** without a 9th Pay Commission, about **Rs 3.19 lakh/month** if a 9th CPC lands in Jan 2036 with a 15% real raise (pure assumption).
- Range: fitment 1.83 gives Rs 1.34 lakh at joining; 2.28 gives Rs 1.67 lakh.
- NPS: you put in 10% of (basic + DA), the government adds 14%.
The full personal 10-year projection (with expenses, other income and net worth) is in the local output folder, not on this portal.

items.q: Why does DA keep increasing as a percentage?
a: **DA is not a raise. It only protects your basic pay from inflation.**
- Basic pay is fixed in the prices of the pay commission's base date (8th CPC: 1 Jan 2026).
- DA (dearness allowance) = the % rise in the 12-month average of CPI-IW (consumer prices for industrial workers) **since that base date**. It's cumulative, so as long as prices rise, it only climbs.
- Revised twice a year (1 Jan, 1 Jul), usually announced about 3 months late with arrears.
- At the next pay commission, the accumulated DA is merged into basic (most of the 'fitment factor'), a real raise goes on top, and DA resets to 0%.
- Under the 7th CPC: 0% in Jan 2016 to 60% in Jan 2026 (about 4.8% a year). Covid froze it Jan 2020-Jun 2021.
- Knock-on effects: HRA steps up when DA crosses 25% and 50%; TA, NPS and gratuity all rise with DA.
Your real raises come from the 3% yearly increment, MACP/promotion, and the real part of each pay commission.

items.q: What does a PGT salary look like over a full career, at age 47 and at retirement?
a: **Model, not fact.** Assumes joining July 2029, 8th CPC fitment 1.92, 6% inflation driving DA, future pay commissions in 2036 and 2046 (+15% real), MACP after 10 and 20 years, no promotion.

- **Last month at 60 (Feb 2055, Level 10, 10th CPC):** gross about Rs 16.8 lakh/month nominal. Basic 48%, DA 32%, HRA 14%, TA 5%.
- DA's share rises through each pay commission cycle and drops back to 0 when it merges into basic.

- Retirement: superannuation at 60. Delhi DoE re-employs teachers up to PGT level till 62 (subject to fitness). Gratuity = 1/4 x (basic + DA) x completed half-years, capped (Rs 25 lakh today). NPS: 60% lump sum tax-free, 40% buys a pension.

items.q: In KVS, how often will I be transferred? Can I stay in Delhi for life once I get transferred there?
a: **There's no automatic rotation, but there's no lifetime Delhi guarantee either.**
- You move only when you request it, when you're displaced, or when KVS needs to fill a vacancy.
- **First posting** can be anywhere. Direct recruits serve 5 years at a normal station before requesting a move.
- **Hard / North-East stations:** 3-year tenure, and **+30 points** towards your next request. The best route back to Delhi.
- **Displacement:** after 5+ years at one station with a displacement count of 10+, you can be moved out to make room for people returning from hard stations.
- Men under 40 who haven't served a hard-station tenure can be moved to fill vacancies.
- Delhi counts as one 'station', so moving between Delhi KVs is not a transfer.
Realistic path: first posting outside Delhi, then request Delhi, then likely many years there, with some displacement risk.

items.q: If I'm posted to a KVS school outside Delhi, how will I commute? Will I rent a flat, or does the government provide accommodation?
a: **You'd live in that town, not commute from Delhi. Either you get a staff quarter, or you rent locally and draw HRA.**

- **Staff quarters:** KVS gives govt accommodation wherever the school has its own quarters, or where the 'sponsoring agency' (the defence, PSU or govt body the KV was opened for) provides them. KVs in cantonments, PSU townships and campuses often have them.
- **Not guaranteed:** the govt told Parliament KVS builds a small set of quarters per school and has no plan to house 100% of staff. KVS had built about 14,700 quarters by 2014.

- **Allotment:** under the KVS (Allotment of Residence) Rules, 1998, by your pay level. You pay a small licence fee and **lose your HRA** while in the quarter. If you refuse an allotted quarter, HRA can be stopped.

- **If there's no quarter:** you rent a flat or room near the school and get **HRA** of 30% / 20% / 10% of basic for X / Y / Z-class cities. At the Level 8 entry basic of Rs 47,600, that's about Rs 14,280 / 9,520 / 4,760 a month.
- **Commute:** there's no transport allowance for living far away. Normal central-govt transport allowance applies, and teachers usually live close to the school.
- **Transfer costs:** when you're transferred, central rules cover moving expenses (transfer TA and a lump-sum grant). Standard rule; to verify for KVS.
Tip: in small towns the HRA is low, so a staff quarter is often the better deal. Ask about quarters when you report.

items.q: How many holidays and leaves does a Delhi PGT get? Is there a two-month summer vacation?
a: **Yes, about 7 weeks off in summer.**
- **Summer vacation 2026:** 11 May - 30 June (51 days). Teachers usually report back 2-3 days early.
- **Autumn break:** about 3 days. **Winter break:** about 1-15 January.
- **Public holidays:** Delhi's official list, plus 2 optional holidays and up to 5 special school holidays.
Catch: principals can call 2-3 teachers in during summer for admissions or office work. If called in, you get earned leave in exchange.
**Leave:**
- Casual leave: 8 days a year (+2 optional holidays)
- Earned leave: **none in a year you take the full vacation** (only if vacation is cut short). This is the trade-off for long breaks.
- Half-pay leave: 20 days per year of service (can become 10 full-pay days for medical reasons)
- Child care leave: 730 days over the career (women, and single fathers)
- Paternity leave: 15 days. Special casual leave: up to 15 days a year for set purposes.

items.q: Where will I be posted in Delhi, what is the actual work, what are the hours, and are Saturday-Sunday off?
a: **Posting:**
- About 1,050 Delhi govt schools plus 37 specialised-excellence schools (2023-24); about 1,250 counting govt-aided.
- The Directorate of Education decides after selection: **anywhere in Delhi, Narela to Najafgarh**. You don't pick. Never outside Delhi.
- Transfers: apply online once a year, after 2 years in a school.
- **Double-shift schools:** girls in the morning (~7 am-12:30 pm), boys in the evening (~1-6:30 pm). As a man you'd often teach the evening boys' shift.
**The work:**
- Economics for Class 11-12 plus CBSE board prep; sometimes lower classes when short-staffed.
- Class teacher duties, PTMs (big ones on Saturdays), admissions, board invigilation and copy checking, trainings, data entry.
- Govt duties outside teaching: election duty, BLO voter-list work (leave given in exchange on holidays), Census 2026-27 work. A NIEPA study found teachers spend only about 19% of time on teaching.
**Hours:** about a 6-6.5 hour school day plus some prep at home. **Sundays off. Saturdays usually off but not guaranteed** (PTMs, remedial classes, trainings; the law needs 220 working days).

**Work-life balance, honestly:** very good among govt jobs (long holidays, short fixed day, security, no targets). Downsides: paperwork, extra duties, possible evening shift, long commute to a school you didn't choose.

- **Vice Principal:** Level 10 (Rs 56,100). Half by promotion, half by direct UPSC recruitment.

items.q: As a PGT, can I publish research papers and give my opinion on government policies?
a: **Research: yes. Criticising government policy: no.** Delhi govt teachers come under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (simple: the code of conduct for central and Delhi govt employees).
**Allowed:**
- Research papers in journals, with a note that the views are your own and no official information used.
- Books and explainers (occasional literary/academic work needs no prior sanction if teaching doesn't suffer; royalty may need declaring).
- Neutral explainers ("how the repo rate works"); seminars and guest lectures (take permission for paid or organised ones).
**Not allowed:**
- **Rule 9:** any statement with the effect of adverse criticism of current or recent government policy, in print, TV, online or speech.
- **Rule 8:** running or editing a newspaper, periodical or media channel needs prior sanction; a regular YouTube channel or newsletter can fall under this.
- **Rule 15:** paid advisory, AUM fees, RIA work, monetised content without sanction. In practice the advisory book can't continue.
- **Rule 16:** frequent buying and selling of securities (F&O, intraday) counts as speculation and is prohibited. Long-term investing is fine.
- **Rule 5:** no political participation.
**For you:** the job would take away your public policy voice, your advisory book and option trading while in service. Neutral research and data explainers survive.

items.q: What is the probation period for a PGT, and how does it differ across recruiters (DSSSB/Delhi DoE, KVS, NVS, EMRS)?
a: **It's 2 years everywhere, and every recruiter can extend it.** No recruiter on your list has a shorter one.

- **Delhi DoE (via DSSSB):** 2 years, extendable by the Appointing Authority. You're made regular only after you complete it successfully. During this time either side can end the job with one month's notice. Recent DSSSB ads also require at least 2 weeks of induction training to complete probation.
- **NDMC (via DSSSB):** follows its own recruitment rules. Probation not yet checked.
- **KVS:** 2 years. You're treated as a trainee, and you're posted as per your preference after it.
- **NVS (Navodaya):** 2 years, extendable. Residential duties (housemaster, supervision) are assessed along with teaching.

- **EMRS (NESTS):** 2 years, extendable. You can be terminated at any time without a reason given. You must also learn the local language of your posting and pass a NESTS language test within probation.
Plain English: probation (simple: a trial period). You get full pay, but the job isn't permanent yet and is easier to end.

items.q: During PGT probation, is there a target? What do they check, and what do I need to do to clear it?
a: **There is no written numeric target (like a fixed pass %) for clearing probation.** The Appointing Authority judges whether you are suitable for the job, using these checks:
- **Induction training:** at least 2 weeks. It is mandatory, and probation can't be completed without it (DoPT rule; also printed in recent DSSSB ads).

- **Probation report + APAR:** your Principal/supervisor writes a separate probation report on top of the yearly APAR (Annual Performance Appraisal Report; simple: your yearly report card). Per DoPT, it covers your work, "outlook, character and aptitude".

- **Documents and verification:** certificates checked against the originals, plus the OBC/NCL certificate, medical fitness, and police verification of character and antecedents. A discrepancy found at any stage cancels the appointment. The Delhi DoE has extended probation by 6 months just to finish this verification.
- **Clean record:** no vigilance case, no departmental enquiry, no penalty.
- **Results (in practice, not a written probation rule):** board results in your subject matter. Delhi DoE has served show-cause notices to schools/teachers for poor results.
- **EMRS extra:** pass the NESTS language test for the local language. Residential duties are assessed too (also in NVS).

**Outcomes:** confirmed, OR extended (max 1 year at a time; never beyond double the normal period, so at most 4 years), OR discharged with no compensation. The decision should come within 6-8 weeks after probation ends. If no order is issued, you simply stay on probation; you are not confirmed automatically.

**Practical checklist:** finish induction training; keep the original certificates + a fresh OBC/NCL ready; get good results in your Class 11-12 Economics sections; no disputes or complaints; take on school duties (exam, admission, events) willingly; make sure your Principal files your APAR/probation report on time; and once 2 years are up, follow up for the confirmation order.

items.q: What are the KRAs (Key Result Areas) of a PGT teacher?
a: **Government schools don't issue a corporate-style KRA sheet.** The closest thing is the **APAR** (Annual Performance Assessment Report; simple: the yearly report card that also feeds probation, confirmation and promotion).

**How the APAR scores you (DoPT-style numerical grading, used by KVS since 2011):** each item is graded 1-10. Overall score = **40% Work Output + 30% Personal Attributes + 30% Functional Competency**. KVS uses a separate form for teachers (Proforma-D).
**The practical KRAs this translates into** (synthesis from the APAR structure + how DoE/KVS act; not an official list):
- **1. Board results (biggest):** Class 12 (and 11) Economics pass % and quality of grades. KVS calculates a Performance Index (PI) per teacher; Delhi DoE issues show-cause notices for poor results.
- **2. Teaching delivery:** finishing the syllabus on time, lesson plans, class tests, remedial classes for weak students.
- **3. Records:** attendance, marks/assessment entry on the portal, result analysis.
- **4. School duties:** exam invigilation and evaluation, admissions, class teacher work, events, CCA (co-curricular activities: debates, quizzes, competitions).
- **5. Government duties:** Delhi teachers are often deployed on census, election (BLO) or survey work.
- **6. Personal attributes:** punctuality, integrity, discipline, relations with students, parents and colleagues.
- **7. Growth:** in-service training, CBSE/SCERT workshops, new methods (NEP 2020 competency-based teaching).

items.q: Compare PGT (DSSSB/KVS) with DU Assistant Professor on everything: entry, pay, probation, KRA, work-life, growth.
a: **DU wins on:** pay (Level 10, Rs 57,700 vs Level 8, Rs 47,600; about Rs 14.5 lakh vs Rs 11.5 lakh CTC, ESTIMATE), no B.Ed, no age limit, a shorter probation (1 year vs 2), retirement at 65 vs 60, 16 hours/week teaching, no board-result pressure, a fixed college with no transfers, and a career top of Professor (L14) vs Principal (L12).

**PGT wins on:** certainty. Selection is an objective written exam where merit decides; DU is interview-only with panel discretion. PGT is also faster and more predictable once the B.Ed is done, and needs no PhD ever.

**Probation:** PGT is 2 years, extendable, with no automatic confirmation. DU is 1 year + at most 1 more; you're confirmed at the end of year 1 unless extended by a specific order, and the confirmation order is due within 45 days (UGC 2018 cl. 11).
**KRA:** PGT is judged by the APAR (40/30/30), with board results dominating. DU uses UGC Table 1: classes taught / assigned (80%+ Good) + 3 or more activities (exam duty, clubs, seminars, research).

**Growth:** DU promotions are time-bound under CAS: L11 after 4 years (with PhD) or 6 years (without), L12 after 5 more, Associate Professor after 3 more (PhD MANDATORY), Professor after 3 more. PGT promotions depend on seniority and vacancies, plus MACP at 10/20/30 years.
**Gate for Ashish:** PGT needs a B.Ed + OBC (Delhi) certificate. DU needs only NET (status to confirm).

items.q: I don't have NET yet. Once I qualify, is it valid for life?
a: **Yes, for Assistant Professor eligibility the NET certificate is valid for life.** You clear it once and can apply for posts for the rest of your career (no upper age limit for Assistant Professor).
**The catch:** since June 2024, NET results come in 3 categories:
- **Category 1, JRF:** Assistant Professor eligibility (lifetime) + funded PhD + PhD admission. The JRF award letter is valid for 3 years.
- **Category 2, Assistant Professor + PhD admission:** Assistant Professor eligibility valid for life.
- **Category 3, PhD admission only:** valid 1 year, and it does **NOT** make you eligible for Assistant Professor. Landing here is not enough.

So the target is Category 2 at minimum. Category 1 (JRF) is worth aiming for: the JRF age limit is 35 for OBC, so you have until about Feb 2030, and JRF adds 2 screening points (52 vs 50) plus a paid PhD route.
Status: NET not held as of 2026-10-02. The next cycle is Dec 2026; the form usually opens around October.

items.q: What is the exam pattern of UGC NET (Economics), and how does it compare with the PGT exams?
a: **UGC NET (run by NTA, twice a year: June and December):** computer-based, one sitting, **3 hours, 150 questions, 300 marks**. +2 per correct answer, **no negative marking**.

- **Paper 1 (common to all subjects), 50 Q / 100 marks:** teaching aptitude, research aptitude, reading comprehension, communication, mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, data interpretation, ICT, people/development/environment, the higher education system. About 5 questions per unit.

- **Paper 2 (Economics), 100 Q / 200 marks, 10 units:** (1) Microeconomics (2) Macroeconomics (3) Statistics & Econometrics (4) Mathematical Economics (5) International Economics (6) Public Economics (7) Money & Banking (8) Growth & Development (9) Environmental Economics & Demography (10) Indian Economy.

- **Result:** to be eligible for Assistant Professor you must clear the minimum (40% aggregate General; 35% OBC-NCL) AND rank inside your category's share of the national 6% pool (see the next Q). Landing in the 'PhD only' category is not enough.

**Compared with PGT:** DSSSB PGT is also 300 marks but has 0.25 negative marking (Section I general 100 + Section II Economics + teaching methodology 200). KVS is two-tier plus an interview/demo. NET is only the eligibility gate; the actual DU job is decided by interview.

**Overlap:** NET Paper 2 and the PGT Economics section share most of the core syllabus (micro, macro, Indian economy, money & banking, public finance), so one preparation serves both tracks. NET goes deeper on econometrics and mathematical economics; PGT adds pedagogy and general awareness.
**For Ashish:** Money & Banking, Macro, International and Indian Economy are his daily work (an advantage). Econometrics, Mathematical Economics and Paper 1 aptitude will need dedicated practice.

items.q: Is the NET 'top 6%' the top 6% of OBC candidates, or of the overall pool?
a: **Neither exactly. The 6% sets the total number of seats, and those seats are then split by category. You compete only with OBC candidates for the OBC seats.**
- **Step 1, minimum marks:** at least 35% aggregate across both papers for OBC-NCL (40% for General).
- **Step 2, total seats:** total qualifiers = 6% of ALL candidates who appeared in both papers (the overall pool, all subjects and categories).

- **Step 3, split:** those seats are divided by Govt of India reservation policy (OBC 27%, UR, SC, ST, EWS, etc.), and per NTA bulletins also subject-wise. The OBC seats in Economics go to the highest-scoring OBC-NCL Economics candidates.

Example (ESTIMATE, illustrative numbers): if 10,000 sit Economics, about 600 qualify; about 27% of those (~162) are OBC seats. You need to rank within the top ~162 of the OBC Economics candidates, which is why the OBC cut-off is usually lower than the General one.
**Your certificate matters:** this is a central exam, so the CENTRAL-format OBC-NCL certificate applies (the format you hold), with a fresh NCL per the bulletin's validity rule.

items.q: If I score 75% in NET, what happens next? Do I give an interview for a PhD, for Assistant Professor, or do I get a permanent job directly?
a: **75% = 225/300. That's above the recent OBC JRF cut-off (212-216), so you'd likely land in Category 1 (JRF).** But NET is an eligibility certificate, **not a job**. Nobody appoints you on the NET score alone.
**What 225 unlocks (three doors, all through an interview):**

- **Door 1, Assistant Professor (the permanent job):** lifetime eligibility. Apply to each DU college advert, screening (about 52 with JRF), then an **interview**. The interview decides the permanent job.

- **Door 2, PhD with JRF:** JRF holders get into a PhD on **interview only** (no entrance test), under the UGC PhD Regulations 2022. Pay: Rs 37,000/month (JRF, years 1-2), then Rs 42,000 (SRF, years 3-5), plus HRA. You must join a PhD within the 3-year validity of the JRF letter.
- **Door 3, PhD without JRF:** Category 2/3 admissions are 70% NET score + 30% interview. Not relevant at 75%.

**The trade-off:** JRF is for full-time PhD scholars, so you generally can't hold a job while drawing it. If you get a permanent Assistant Professor post first, you give up the fellowship but can do a PhD while teaching (you'll need it later for Associate Professor).

**Suggested sequence (ESTIMATE):** clear NET with JRF, then apply to DU college adverts straight away AND apply for a PhD (e.g. Delhi School of Economics, JNU). If a permanent post comes first, take it and do the PhD while working. If not, take the JRF-funded PhD: it raises your screening score to about 77 (PhD = 25 points), which makes the next interviews far easier.
**PGT track:** NET doesn't count for PGT. The B.Ed is still required, but the Economics preparation overlaps.
**Open point:** JRF rules on outside income would affect the advisory book and your job. Check before you accept JRF.

items.q: How can I become the Principal of a DU college?
a: **A DU college Principal is selected through an advert and interview, not promoted by seniority. UGC 2018 eligibility (Professor's grade, Level 14):**
- PhD (mandatory)
- Already an Associate Professor or Professor, with **at least 15 years** of teaching/research in universities, colleges or higher-education institutions
- At least **10 research publications** in peer-reviewed / UGC-listed journals
- A **research score of 110+** (UGC Appendix II, Table 2)

**Tenure:** 5 years, extendable once by 5 years after a performance review. After that you return as a Professor. The Vice Principal is a senior teacher the Governing Body designates for 2 years, not a separate post.

**Realistic path for Ashish (ESTIMATE):** NET with JRF (2027), then Assistant Professor + PhD (permanent post realistically around age 34-38), then CAS to Associate Professor (about 12 years in; PhD mandatory), with publications accumulating along the way, then eligible for Principal at about 15 years of service, i.e. around age 49-53. DU teachers retire at 65 (to verify), so there's roughly a 12-16 year window to compete for Principal posts.

**What decides it:** the PhD + research record (publications, research score, PhD students guided), administrative experience (committees, coordinator/Vice Principal roles), and the Governing Body / selection committee interview.

**PGT comparison:** a school Principal (Level 12) is reached mainly by promotion (PGT, then Vice Principal, then Principal), with no PhD or publications needed. The DU Principal post is a higher grade (Level 14) but much more research-heavy.

items.q: Explain the whole DU professor saga step by step: NET, JRF ('GRF'), PhD, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor. My only aim is to become a permanent professor at DU.
a: **'GRF' is JRF (Junior Research Fellowship).** It's the top result band in UGC NET: a paid PhD (Rs 37,000/month for years 1-2, then Rs 42,000 as SRF for years 3-5, plus HRA) on top of Assistant Professor eligibility.
**The pieces, in plain English:**

- **UGC NET:** an eligibility test, not a job. Category 1 = JRF + Asst Prof + PhD admission; Category 2 = Asst Prof + PhD admission; Category 3 = PhD admission only (does NOT make you eligible for Asst Prof).

- **PhD:** a 3-6 year research degree (UGC PhD Regulations 2022). NOT needed to become Assistant Professor; MANDATORY for Associate Professor and above. Can be done part-time while teaching (with employer NOC).
- **Assistant Professor:** the entry rank and the only realistic door into a permanent DU job. Master's 55% (50% OBC-NCL) + NET (or PhD). Selection by interview after screening.
- **Associate Professor:** middle rank. Reached by CAS promotion (PhD + 3 yrs at Level 12), or by direct recruitment (PhD + 8 yrs teaching + 7 publications + research score 75).

- **Professor:** top rank. CAS: 3 yrs as Associate + PhD + 10 publications + research score 110. Direct: PhD + 10 publications + research score 120 (+10 yrs experience). Senior Professor (Level 15) exists only in university departments.

**The pay ladder (UGC 2018, entry pay):** Asst Prof Level 10 Rs 57,700, then Level 11 Rs 68,900 (after 4 yrs with PhD / 6 yrs without), then Level 12 Rs 79,800 (after 5 more yrs), then Associate Level 13A Rs 1,31,400 (after 3 more yrs, PhD required), then Professor Level 14 Rs 1,44,200 (after 3 more yrs). Minimum about 15 years from joining to Professor, with a PhD.

**'Permanent professor':** colloquially any permanent teacher is called 'professor'. Practically, 'permanent' means getting a regular (substantive) Assistant Professor post; after 1-year probation it is secure to age 65, and Associate/Professor then come by CAS promotion from inside.
**Screening score (DU colleges, out of 100; floor 50):** Ashish with NET = 50, with JRF = 52, with PhD + JRF = about 77. Departments need 65+, so a PhD is effectively needed there.

**Sequence for Ashish (ESTIMATE):** (1) NET Dec 2026 / Jun 2027, aim for JRF (OBC JRF age limit 35, ~Feb 2030); (2) apply to every DU college Economics advert immediately; (3) register for a PhD in parallel (JRF-funded full-time, or part-time once employed); (4) permanent post realistically 3-8 years out; (5) CAS: Associate ~12 yrs in, Professor ~15 yrs in.

**PGT comparison:** PGT ladder is PGT (Level 8) to Vice Principal (Level 10) to Principal (Level 12), mostly seniority, no PhD or publications. DU ladder goes to Level 14/15 but is research-gated from the Associate stage.

items.q: To sit for UGC NET, do I need a Master's degree?
a: **Yes, for the Assistant Professor route a Master's is required.** UGC NET eligibility: Master's with 55% (50% for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD). Final-year PG students can also apply, but must finish the Master's with the required marks within 2 years of the NET result.

**Exception:** since 2024, a 4-year undergraduate (FYUP / honours with research) with 75% can sit NET without a Master's, but that opens JRF / PhD admission. For Assistant Professor eligibility, the UGC 2018 rule still asks for Master's 55% + NET.
**Ashish:** PG in Economics already done and meets the 55% condition, so he is eligible to sit NET now. NET is the only missing gate for DU.
**PGT comparison:** DSSSB PGT also needs a Master's (50%+ in Economics), but no NET; its missing gate is the B.Ed. So the Master's is common to both tracks; DU adds NET, PGT adds B.Ed.

items.q: To sit UGC NET, do I need a Master's (MA) degree, or is it not required?
a: **Yes, a Master's is the normal requirement, and you already have it.**
- **Master's route:** 55% in the Master's (50% for OBC-NCL/SC/ST/PwD). This makes you eligible for all three NET outcomes, including Assistant Professor.
- **Final-year Master's students** can also sit, but must finish the Master's within 2 years of the result.
- **4-year UG (honours/research) with 75%:** can sit NET, but only for JRF/PhD. NOT eligible for Assistant Professor, which still needs the Master's 55%.
- **Plain 3-year graduation with no Master's:** cannot sit NET.
**PGT comparison:** PGT also needs the Master's (50%), plus a B.Ed. NET needs no B.Ed.
